dedupe_keys.name: instad djibouti third general population and housing census rgph 3 2024 thematic volume 15 on households and housing with drinking water electricity sanitation waste internet and energy producing assets by region

description: INSTAD Djibouti published the results of its third general population and housing census, held in 2024, as 22 thematic PDF volumes on its RGPH page in November 2025. Volume 15 covers households, housing and living conditions. Its housing chapter gives dwelling type and building materials, tenure and crowding, the main source of drinking water, the main source of lighting energy, cooking fuel, toilets, washing facilities and the disposal of waste water and household refuse. The assets chapter adds internet access, transport means and energy-producing assets. National indicators include 90.7 percent of ordinary households with safe water, 72.6 percent with electricity, 64 percent with internet and 11.8 percent owning a solar panel; grid supply from EDD reaches 71.4 percent of households in Djibouti city against 16.5 percent in Tadjourah. Coverage is national, with tables by region and urban or rural area. Format and access: free PDFs, no registration. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: tables are percentages inside PDFs; the site is a script app, and the file list came from the JSON feed behind it. Simulation uses: regional electrification and water supply gaps, off-grid solar uptake, and housing fragility. Related records: none for Djibouti in the catalogue.

schema_summary: Chapter 6 housing: dwelling type, roof, wall and floor material, tenure, crowding, main drinking water source and access to safe water (tables 49 to 50), main lighting energy and access to electricity (51 to 52), kitchen and cooking fuel, toilet type and sharing, washing facility, waste water and solid waste disposal (58 to 59), housing precariousness. Chapter 7 assets: ICT equipment, internet access and mode (62 to 64), transport means, energy-producing assets such as solar panels and generators, appliances, livestock and farmland. Tables break down by region, urban or rural, sex, age, education and living standard of the household head.
